clue.text: More of an extravagant display by David Hockney

definitions.meaning: a showier, more lavish public show, in the comparative
the title of Hockney's 1967 painting of a swimming-pool splash in California

explanation.surface: Someone is praised for an even showier display than David Hockney managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a splash is an idiom for a showy entrance, and Hockney's famous pool painting carries the same title.

clue.text: Richard Strauss version of The Sound of Music?

definitions.text: Richard Strauss version of The Sound of Music?

parts.words: Richard Strauss version of The Sound of Music?
parts.note: the musical is set in the Austrian mountains, so a mountain-themed orchestral work by Strauss is jokingly its counterpart

explanation.surface: A mischievous question about Richard Strauss scoring a Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's 1915 tone poem depicts a day climbing a mountain, so it is literally music sounding of the high peaks.

clue.text: French composer, I wager, is right inside

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right goes within the word for wager

parts.note: to wager is to bet

explanation.surface: A French composer gambles on being correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a twentieth-century French composer, known for his Escales.

clue.text: Shame Genet, perhaps, in biblical garden

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the two words might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: The French playwright Jean Genet is somehow shamed in a garden from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Genet looks like a name the solver must know about, but it is just letters: SHAME plus GENET rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prayed before his arrest.

clue.text: Pianist is better off holding model

indicators.note: holding says the word for better off contains the letter for model

parts.note: someone better off is richer
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A pianist is said to be wealthier for having a model in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Sviatoslav Richter was a celebrated Soviet concert pianist.

clue.text: "Implores the — tribute of a sigh" (Gray)

parts.note: fill in the missing word from Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, where humble graves ask for a sigh from those going by

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Gray's Elegy with one word blanked out.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Elegy the tribute is one offered by a fleeting passer-by, so the gap takes the adjective for going by.

clue.text: Morning the French came back in battle

indicators.note: came back says the morning and the French pieces are both read backwards

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A soldier returns one morning from fighting alongside the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns the whole run AMLA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1854 Crimean War battle where British and French forces defeated the Russians at the river of that name.

clue.text: Strangely, our bard he was sheltered

indicators.note: strangely says the following letters come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Oddly, the poet was given shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link; the anagram of OUR BARD HE gives the past tense meaning gave shelter to.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour is to give refuge or protection, as a port protects ships.

clue.text: A fine cameo from Gower, perhaps (or R. S. Thomas)

definitions.text: A fine cameo from Gower, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a pretty view of the Gower peninsula in south Wales, Gower being one example
a poem by the Welsh poet R. S. Thomas with this title

explanation.surface: A small fine picture of the Gower countryside, or perhaps a poem by R. S. Thomas.
explanation.walkthrough: Gower could be the medieval poet John Gower, but here it is the Welsh peninsula near Swansea.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic vista of Wales describes a Gower view, and Thomas's poem of that name broods on Welsh history.

clue.text: Dark in The Timeless Land portrays old-time novices?

definitions.text: Dark in The Timeless Land portrays
definitions.meaning: Eleanor Dark's Australian novel The Timeless Land features convicts of this surname

explanation.surface: The novelist Eleanor Dark depicts beginners in her historical novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Dark is the Australian author Eleanor Dark, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprentices were once commonly called by this clipped form, as in Elizabethan London's unruly youths, and Dark gave it to characters.

clue.text: Endeavour's code from Colin Dexter

definitions.meaning: the dots-and-dashes signalling system, sharing a name with Endeavour, the detective's first name
Dexter wrote the Oxford detective novels featuring Inspector Endeavour of that surname

explanation.surface: A secret code belonging to someone called Endeavour, invented by Colin Dexter.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel's telegraph code and Dexter's inspector, whose rarely used first name is Endeavour, share one surname.

clue.text: South wind (for you, perhaps, but we decline)

definitions.meaning: the Greek god of the south wind

definitions.text: for you, perhaps, but we decline
definitions.meaning: a phrase refusing on our behalf while allowing others: not for ourselves

explanation.surface: A southerly breeze may suit you, but we turn it down.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the deity of the moist southern wind; split in two it reads as a refusal for ourselves.

clue.text: Small recital group could make a riot

indicators.note: could make says the letters of the next word can be rearranged to form a new one

explanation.surface: A small group of performers might cause a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link; only the four letters of RIOT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber ensemble of three players, small enough for a recital.

clue.text: Five circle ship in White book

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
O is circle-shaped
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Five circles around a ship in a book that is white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' is Patrick White, the Australian Nobel laureate; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Patrick White's 1957 novel about a German explorer crossing the Australian interior.

clue.text: Portmanteau for bringing back souvenirs in old age?

definitions.text: Portmanteau for bringing back souvenirs in old age?

parts.words: Portmanteau for bringing back souvenirs in old age?
parts.note: a portmanteau is both a travel bag and a blended word; this blend joins a word for short stories told about the past with a word for senility

explanation.surface: A suitcase for carrying holiday mementoes home in one's twilight years.
explanation.walkthrough: Souvenirs here means memories, as in French, and portmanteau means a blended word rather than luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular coinage for the stage of life when someone constantly reminisces, blending a tale-telling noun with senility.

clue.text: Dickens army surgeon in prison

definitions.meaning: Doctor of that name, the touchy regimental surgeon in The Pickwick Papers

explanation.surface: A Dickensian army doctor ends up behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang term for jail, from doors slamming shut, and the hot-tempered doctor in Pickwick.

clue.text: Disoriented Dorset pal recalled by Thomas

indicators.note: disoriented says the letters have lost their bearings and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confused friend from Dorset is remembered by someone named Thomas.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas is Edward Thomas, whose poem opens 'Yes. I remember' this Gloucestershire village railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Thomas's best-known poem recalls a train halting briefly at that village station one June afternoon.

clue.text: How Keaton's classic engine was ranked

definitions.text: How Keaton's classic engine was ranked

parts.words: How Keaton's classic engine was ranked
parts.note: Buster Keaton's 1926 silent comedy is named after the stolen locomotive at its centre, a name that is also a high military rank

explanation.surface: A question of where Buster Keaton's famous locomotive stood in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The locomotive in Keaton's film bears a name that is also the top rank in an army.

clue.text: Scarlett saved her life

parts.note: in Gone with the Wind, Scarlett O'Hara delivers her sister-in-law's baby and gets her out of burning Atlanta

explanation.surface: Scarlett rescued a woman from death.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashley Wilkes's wife in Margaret Mitchell's novel, whom Scarlett nursed through childbirth during the siege of Atlanta.

clue.text: Hilda's brother, a bit of a shrimp

definitions.meaning: the boy whose elder sister is Hilda in L. P. Hartley's novels
in Hartley's The Shrimp and the Anemone, the timid boy is likened to the shrimp

explanation.surface: Hilda's brother is a little on the small side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hartley's trilogy follows a sensitive boy dominated by his sister, cast as the shrimp to her anemone.

clue.text: Club professor in ancient kingdom

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A professor wields a club in an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingdom of Philip II and Alexander the Great in northern Greece.

clue.text: Czech composer of a drink, almost (I will leave it for you, say)

indicators.note: will leave it says the letter I departs from the drink

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail
the clue's own I is the letter removed
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A Czech composer is nearly a drink, which I will leave to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' and 'I will leave it' together say one letter, I, drops from the end of the cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinů was a prolific twentieth-century Czech composer of symphonies and operas.

clue.text: Wells's long-suffering headmaster seen in the still flickering flames

definitions.meaning: Job of that surname, the afflicted schoolmaster in H. G. Wells's The Undying Fire

definitions.text: seen in the still flickering flames
definitions.meaning: the Czech reformer Jan of this name was burned at the stake in 1415

explanation.surface: A suffering headmaster from H. G. Wells appears in a dying fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells modelled his schoolmaster on Job, and the Bohemian reformer of the same name died at the stake.

clue.text: Ruler in limits arbitrarily set

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: A ruler sets limits on his subjects at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a link; the run straddles the end of 'limits' and the start of 'arbitrarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Examinations alternative as student is included

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: is included says the student letter goes inside as

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: An alternative set of tests in which a student takes part.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken tests, like a viva, rather than written papers.

clue.text: "A board of oysters, or o'rizzered haddies" (John Wilson)

definitions.text: "A board of oysters, or o'rizzered haddies" (John Wilson)

parts.words: "A board of oysters, or o'rizzered haddies" (John Wilson)
parts.note: a line from John Wilson's Noctes Ambrosianae with a Scots word for a serving platter replaced by board; rizzered haddies are sun-dried haddock

explanation.surface: A Scottish quotation offering oysters or dried haddock on a platter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a large oval serving dish, from French assiette, a plate.

clue.text: Continent initially almost significant in Albee

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Edward Albee's work is said to be almost wholly continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the world's landmasses.

clue.text: Early Scandinavian practitioners of spin

parts.note: in Norse myth three women spin the threads of fate, a pun on modern political spin doctors

explanation.surface: Old Norse spin doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse fates who spin and weave the destinies of gods and men at the roots of Yggdrasil.

clue.text: Birthplace of first-century bowl importer

parts.note: legend says Joseph, from this town in Judea, brought the Holy Grail to Glastonbury in England

explanation.surface: Home town of an early trader who brought in bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowl is the Holy Grail and the importer is the Joseph who buried Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Judean town named as Joseph's home in the Gospels.

clue.text: Square hillock portrayed by Utrillo

definitions.meaning: in French the name means the square of the mound
Maurice Utrillo painted many Montmartre street scenes, including this square

explanation.surface: A square mound painted by Utrillo.
explanation.definitionFit: The artists' square at the top of Montmartre in Paris, whose name means the square of the knoll.
